item.title: Shapiro on data center order: "I don't want developers running roughshod"
item.description: "We've seen too many developers who are trying to bulldoze our community," Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro told "CBS Mornings."

item.title: Details on potential motive behind Tupac's murder
item.description: Duane "Keffe D" Davis, who is accused of orchestrating the 1996 murder of Tupac Shakur, is back in court for the third day of his trial as more details emerge on the potential motive behind the fatal shooting. CBS News' Katrina Kaufman has more.

item.title: Watch Live: Lindsay Clancy trial resumes with cross-examination of psychologist
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's trial​ resumed Wednesday in Massachusetts with the cross-examination of a psychologist who testified that Clancy said she heard a voice ordering her to kill her children.

item.title: Ukraine's fired defense minister calls for elections despite war with Russia
item.description: The former defense minister, whose firing sparked weeks of protests, said Ukraine needed to find a way to hold elections despite the prolonged war with Russia.

item.title: "Recess Therapy" creator on why adults should bring child-like behavior back into their lives
item.description: Julian Shapiro-Barnum is known for his conversations with kids on his series "Recess Therapy." He tells "CBS Mornings" why he thinks adults need to act more childish and embrace some behaviors of children.

item.title: Florida democratic socialist Angie Nixon says "it's not about labels"
item.description: Florida state Rep. Angie Nixon defeated Alex Vindman in Tuesday's primary, setting up the race against GOP Sen. Ashley Moody in November.

item.title: Isla Fisher on what "Spa Weekend" meant to her and importance of female friendships
item.description: Isla Fisher gives an inside look at the new film, "Spa Weekend," how it highlights the importance of female friendships and how the star-studded cast connected.

item.title: Iran's top diplomat and Trump cast doubt on any hope for a peace deal
item.description: Iran's foreign minister says Tehran is interested only in a deal to fully end the war, not a ceasefire, after Trump says there's currently no dialogue at all.

item.title: Should you pay collections debt that's past the statute of limitations?
item.description: An old collections balance may have lost its legal bite, but paying it could come with unintended consequences.

item.title: Maps and charts show record number of measles cases in U.S. this year
item.description: CBS News has been tracking a record number of measles cases and outbreaks around the country. The majority of cases are among those who haven't been vaccinated.

item.title: Scandal-ridden Cory Mills ousted in GOP primary in Florida's 7th District
item.description: The Trump-backed incumbent has struggled to raise money for his reelection bid as the House Ethics Committee investigates numerous allegations against him.

item.title: Exclusive discounts from CBS Mornings Deals
item.description: On this edition of CBS Mornings Deals, we show you items that will help improve your everyday lifestyle. Visit cbsdeals.com to take advantage of these exclusive deals today. CBS earns commissions on purchases made through cbsdeals.com.

item.title: Data center restriction in Pennsylvania is badly needed, anti-pollution advocate says
item.description: Communities across the U.S. are grappling with data center development projects. Matthew Mehalik, the Breathe Project executive director, joins CBS News after Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro placed guardrails on data center development for his state.

item.title: Dangerous heat dome causes extreme temperatures in the South
item.description: There were record-high temperatures on Tuesday in six states as a dangerous heat dome causes extreme temperatures in parts of the U.S. Rob Marciano has the latest.

item.title: How parents can teach their kids good financial habits
item.description: CBS News business analyst Jill Schlesinger joins "CBS Mornings" to give advice on how to create strong financial foundations and habits for your kids.

item.title: Democratic socialist Angie Nixon on her win in Florida, major issues and message for midterms
item.description: Florida state legislator Angie Nixon, a democratic socialist, talks with "CBS Mornings" about her upset victory in the state's Democratic Senate primary. She addresses major issues facing Americans, her views on aid to Israel and if the democratic socialist message will resonate in a general election.

item.title: Justice Department to send a record 1,000 monitors to midterm polling places
item.description: The Justice Department is planning to deploy a record 1,000 federal monitors to polling places throughout the U.S. for the midterm elections.

item.title: Inflation is outpacing wages again. Many workers were already behind.
item.description: When inflation rises faster than workers' wages, it feels like they're getting a pay cut. Companies, meanwhile, benefit.

item.title: DEI policies brought no financial penalty to firms, study finds
item.description: Companies that stood by their diversity efforts faced no detectable impact from investors or shoppers, researchers found.

item.title: Man has "miracle" recovery after heart defect causes rare massive stroke
item.description: One year after a massive stroke nearly incapacitated him, Todd Meiklejohn is opening up about his experience.

item.title: She went to "hell and back" for a diagnosis. Then her sister showed symptoms.
item.description: Megan Koverman's weight gain, fatigue, high blood pressure and other symptoms were dismissed for years before she was diagnosed with a rare heart disease.

item.title: Grandfather with pancreatic cancer beats the odds with clinical trial
item.description: Hernando Salcedo was diagnosed with Stage 3 pancreatic cancer after mild symptoms. Chemotherapy made him feel worse than before his diagnosis.

item.title: Pregnant mom diagnosed with Stage 4 cancer after symptoms were dismissed
item.description: Jenney Bitner feared she wouldn't get to see her children grow up after a tumor in her brain revealed she had Stage 4 melanoma.

item.title: Strange symptom leads to man's Stage 4 cancer diagnosis
item.description: An app notification informed Joe Gillette that he had been diagnosed with aggressive, late-stage cancer.

item.title: Her Stage 4 cancer had no symptoms. Innovative surgery saved her life.
item.description: A chance emergency room visit led to Amy Piccoli's diagnosis with late-stage colorectal cancer.

item.title: Four sisters diagnosed with rare brain condition: "Got to be kidding"
item.description: Ashlee and Paul Higginbotham's baby wouldn't stop crying. An MRI found an unusual condition. Soon, they found three of their other children had it too.

item.title: Woman diagnosed with breast cancer at 27 after almost ignoring symptom
item.description: Marissa Coreno didn't think anything about the lump under her armpit at first, until an ultrasound showed something worrying.

item.title: He had 2 months to live. Research "like science fiction" saved his life.
item.description: Michael Wolff was at the "edge of a cliff" when he was diagnosed with a cancer that affects less than 300 patients a year in the U.S.

item.title: After son was born with a rare condition, father donates a kidney
item.description: Jaren Munari was born with just one undersized kidney. After years of watching him suffer from chronic kidney disease, his father donated an organ.

item.title: After an MS diagnosis, this man started running marathons
item.description: Derek Stefureac has reversed the progression of his multiple sclerosis by embracing exercise, doctors said.
